cut_items.item: Explicit warning not to delete anything else in /var/lib/postgresql except via PostgreSQL commands
Notes that wrong pg_wal deletion can also break replicas and recovery (not only corruption)
Command to compare sizes of pg_wal, base, and logs directly
pg_rotate_logfile() to rotate a huge active log
Find root cause of log growth (log_statement='all', error loop)
Check pg_stat_replication for lagging replicas / long-running transactions
Run CHECKPOINT after fixing cause so WAL is removed; space may take minutes to return
Query to find largest tables via pg_total_relation_size
Explains VACUUM vs VACUUM FULL (VACUUM doesn't shrink disk; FULL locks table and needs space)
Extend the volume as fast fallback when space cannot be freed
Verify target of below 80% usage, and note cause plus add lower-threshold (75%) alert
Explicit escalation triggers: >95% usage, PostgreSQL stopped, unsure about dropping slot
Warning that a full disk stops PostgreSQL (urgency)
Rotate an oversized active log with pg_rotate_logfile() instead of deleting it
Find and fix the root cause of log growth (e.g., log_statement='all', error loop)
Check long-running transactions / pg_stat_replication for lagging replicas as a cause of WAL retention
Run CHECKPOINT after fixing cause so PostgreSQL removes old WAL; space may take minutes to return
Fallback: extend the volume if space cannot be freed quickly, safer than manual deletion
Warning not to delete anything else in /var/lib/postgresql except via PostgreSQL commands
Query to list the largest tables (pg_total_relation_size)
Explanation that plain VACUUM only makes space reusable and does not shrink disk; VACUUM FULL shrinks but locks the table
Verification target of below 80% and check that no slot is stuck / no new archiver failures
Post-incident follow-up: document cause and add a lower-threshold (75%) alert
Explicit escalation criteria: usage above 95%, PostgreSQL stopped, or unsure about dropping a slot
Goal/context: if the disk fills PostgreSQL stops
Use wildcard path /var/lib/postgresql/*/pg_wal and du comparison of pg_wal, base, logs to choose the section
Note that a replica whose slot is dropped cannot resume; restart a merely-down replica so it catches up

added_items.item: Also forbids moving or editing pg_wal files, and says corruption can prevent startup
Warning not to run VACUUM FULL on nearly full disk because it needs extra space
Per-command expected results (what output to look for, e.g. inactive slot with old restart_lsn, failed_count/last_failed_time)
du -x command with sudo to list largest directories 3 levels deep
Ask the data owner to archive/purge old rows
Assumptions: psql superuser access, adjust connection options and paths
Explains WAL is write-ahead log, removed by PostgreSQL at next checkpoint after slot drop
Command to find largest directories under /var/lib/postgresql (du --max-depth=3 sorted)
Warning not to run VACUUM FULL on a nearly full disk because it needs extra space to copy the table
Dropping a replication slot makes PostgreSQL remove freed WAL at next checkpoint
Assumption that psql is run as superuser and paths/connection options must be adjusted
Ask data owner to archive or purge old rows for large tables
Explicit instruction not to move or edit pg_wal files either
